headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage if agentic-flow feeds content into Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing/search pipeline.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, and agent_b runs vendor-hosted browsing/search with uploaded documents and browsing context. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if agent_a forwards untrusted text into agent_b. The pair is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF agent_a forwards raw file or prompt content into agent_b without provenance tags, injection becomes plausible.
IF agent_b treats retrieved text or uploaded documents as instructions, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter/provenance wrapper around all agent_a-to-agent_b content.
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in retrieved text.
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like strings before enabling the pair.
Use a fixed schema for outputs from agent_a to agent_b.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches task prompts, repository metadata, code, and Ed25519 signatures; agent_b touches uploaded documents and browsing context and sends queries to vendor APIs. If the pair shares a workspace or forwards sensitive material from agent_a into agent_b, leakage can occur in default workflows. The closed-source vendor backend makes the blast radius broader than local-only tools.
conditions: IF agent_a passes secrets, code, or repository metadata into agent_b uploads or queries, those data classes can leave the local boundary.
IF both agents are used on the same user workspace, cross-agent exposure becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any agent_b upload or query.
Route agent_a outputs through a redaction step before handoff.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Turn off sharing of raw prompts and logs between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the orchestrator boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, modify git state, install packages, and use MCP; agent_b cannot write files or modify git, but it can browse and run browsers. There is no direct write-write conflict, yet if both are pointed at the same repo or workspace, agent_a’s mutable actions can race with agent_b’s read/browse-driven decisions. Uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout, agent_a can mutate state while agent_b reads stale context.
IF agent_b’s browser-driven actions depend on files agent_a is changing, coordination errors can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working copies to each agent.
Pause agent_b while agent_a is mutating git state.
Use a lock file around repo mutations.
Have agent_b read only immutable snapshots.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate analysis and modify repository state; agent_b is a search/RAG system that can incorporate browsing context and uploaded documents. If agent_b treats agent_a’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream answers or actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without independent verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF agent_a’s generated content is later cited or acted on by agent_b, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require a verification step before agent_b uses agent_a output.
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted by default.
Cross-check key claims against primary sources.
Limit agent_a output to structured summaries.
requires-engineering: add confidence/provenance propagation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles repository metadata, task prompts, and signatures; agent_b handles uploaded documents and browsing context through a vendor-hosted service. If regulated or sensitive data is routed from agent_a into agent_b, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or confidential repository data is uploaded to agent_b, vendor-hosted processing may create a policy mismatch.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to agent_a outputs, agent_b’s separate policy must be checked.
mitigations: Do not send regulated data to agent_b.
Review the vendor privacy policy before use.
Keep a data-class allowlist for handoffs.
Separate compliance-sensitive tasks from general search tasks.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
